newsitem.title: USA: Dominick's sets 6.4 million share IPO.
newsitem.headline: Dominick's sets 6.4 million share IPO.

text.p: Dominick's Supermarkets Inc said on Monday that it plans to sell up to 6.4 million common shares in its initial public offering.

The second largest supermarket operator in Chicago, in an amended filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, said that, of the total, 5.9 million shares will be sold by the company and 500,000 shares by some stockholders.

The offering is estimated to be priced between $16 and $18 per share, the filing said. The offering will be made through Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette Securities Corp, Morgan Stanley & Co Inc, BT Securities Corp and Chase Securities Inc.
The selling stockholders have granted the underwriters an over-allotment option of up to 960,000 additional shares.
The company said it would have 21,359,035 common shares outstanding after the offer.

Of the estimated net proceeds to the Company of $92.7 million, about $51.7 million will be used to repurchase the company's outstanding 15 percent redeemable Exchangeable Cumulative Preferred stock, among others, the filing said.
Dominick's stock has been approved for listing on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol "DFF."
